I suppose it's a lot better than your previous map, but there are still many things to work on. I think what a player would find most annoying is the trap doors. They do nothing whatsoever; it only forces the player to start all over again. That is definetely a negative for a map like this. Also, there were many sections of the map that weren't used at all, examples being the thwumps and the mines, they were useless!

With the gold, the pattern was very random, and didn't appeal to me on bit. Try spicing it up a little. You could try fooling around with quarter snap and see if you can come up with a pattern you like.

Lastly, the map was extremely easy to complete. The drones and floor guards were very easy to beat, you should try experimenting with different enemies in the same areas to see which one is the most effective. A good tileset is crucial too. It can be very difficult to create a good map out of a bad tileset. Hope this helps!

Quote: 321southpaw, August 09, 2007 04:26 am
Quote: incluye, August 09, 2007 01:59 am
okay, this is driving me nuts.  How do you guys make those backgrounds?  I got the pictures of Sora just fine.  But I can't make the backgrounds.
Just PM me with some help.  Or tell me how.  Better yet, give me a step-by-step guide.
Step 1: Go to deviantArt.com

Step 2: Find a brush set that says "Abstract" somewhere within the title

Step 3: Download and add to your brushes folder

Step 4: Experiment

Step 5: Practice patience. You might get a good background on your first try, but the next ten will be more difficult, and then they will get easier (I approximated the numbers, but you get my gist)

That is really all there is to it. Imaging is all about practice, patience, and persistence.

Oh yes. He basically summed it all up there. And once you get the hand of brushes, try different styles of putting them in. For example, fill your 1/2 up with the brushes you want. Then invert the whole thing, and apply the same brushes. They will look different. Mess around with the opacity of brushes as well, as some brushes do come in a very dark color.

Okay, figured it out. How do I use new brushes with GIMP?

For me:

C: Drive (or whatever your hard drive is called) -> Program Files -> GIMP 2.0 or something -> share -> gimp -> 2.0 -> brushes

When you open the brushes folder, all of your brushes will be there. Drag and drop your brushes into that folder. Restart GIMP and the brushes will be there.

#356769 14 2007-08-18T17:58:26Z T3chno
Quote: spoon, August 18, 2007 12:14 pm
1-3 are "meh" 6 is awesome though. Also, how do you use gimp? I downloaded it, but I have no idea how to use it

1. First off, you might need to get some good brushes:
GIMP Brushes - DeviantART
2. Download and extract brushes.
3. Go to My computer->C:// (or you main hard drive)->Program File->Gimp->Share->gimp->2.0->brushes
4. Now place the brushes you extracted in that folder.
5. Open up GIMP and then click "New."
6. Set the dimensions to around 450x150.
7. Press brush and open up the menu on the bottom and find any one of the brushes that you just got.
8. Now place the brush and click once where you want it.
9. Now repeat steps 7. and 8. until the sig is halway full.
10. Now pres Shift+F. ---What this does it that it flips the sig horizontally. Now you can use the same brush but it will have a different look.
11. Now after putting burshes in, make a new white layer.
12. To simply give it color, go to the GIMP interface window. There should be 2 boxes one black and one white double click each and set a color for them. They can be different, but try to match colors (which I suck at ).
13. Then select the gradient tool
14. Leave opacity at 100, and in the list, the selection should be FG to BG (RBG).
15. You should experiment with the gradients tool now. Click on the sig and drag a line in any direction and see what the result it. If you don't like it, Ctrl+Z to undo and do a different one. Find one you like.
16. Press Ctrl+L. There should be 2 Layers. Click the New Layer and there should be a list in this small window. Open the list and find overlay. Select overlay.
17. Now you should see your sig in color now.
18. In the window with the sig, go to the userbar on top and click Image then Flatten Image.
19. To add text, click the "T" icon on the GIMP interface window. On the bottom, select your font and click somewhere in th sig and type it in. You can always change the color with the button near where you selected size and font.
20. Flatten Image again and save it. And you're done! Mess around with this as it is just a guide to see where to go and where the buttons are.

~Any questions just ask me. But don't ask me ANYTHING about font. You're better off asking someone else about that.

Also, heres another way to colorize and make your image a lil more sharper:

1) Create new image
2) Do your brush thing
3) then duplicate the layer
4) filters > Blur > garssian blur
5) put both boxes to 13 then press OK
6) go the the layers dialoug then press overlay
7) Merge Down
8) then go to tools > colorize
9) Move the bars back and forth to you get it to what you like

Try not to bring the light bar lower than 0. Bring the hue bar up to make the color brighter. The top bar is just for picking your color.

If you want to colorize a new layer, create a new one and make sure its WHITE. Then go to the layers dialoug and press multiply. It will show the last layer and you are still able to colorize it. If you dont make the background white, it wont colorize well.

Damn... This was a long, guess im bored. Hope this helped in some way.

#17431 1 2007-10-05T04:10:51Z T3chno
Well here it is:

I was doing my homework and my mom turns on the TV. I'm Indian, and my mom has subscribed to the Zee TV channel (an Indian tv channel which has soap operas and game shows). Anyways, she was watching a singing game show, which is REALLY big in India. When the show is over, the soap operas begin. I stop and take a look at the soap.
The scene:
RECAP: -lady stealthily walks into room- She snoops around for any info. She finds a purse. Episode ends.

This episode: She opens purse in slow motion. ~In 5 minutes, she opened the purse. BUT~ a man comes in. Just happens to be her partner in crime. Now. The man stares at purse. You see their faces in shock. What is in there?......-commercial break-.
`After break - More dramatic shock faces. Lady slowly puts her hand in the bag. Man grabs lady's hand. He says "careful. Who knows what might be in there." She SLOWLY pulls out here hand. And in her hand is...............................MONEY! What a surprise finding money in a purse. THe man and lady turn to each other in shock once again. -commercial break-
`After break - Someone is trying to get in the house. He/She opens the door, slowly. The thieves run out, but the weird thing is, the thieves are running at normal speed while the door is opening at half the human speed. Door is just about ot be open and show the face, but it freezes. [/end of episode]

That was the whole episode. Open purse -> hand in purse -> find money -> open door -> end

What a waste of time.

I'll just post here what he said:[He's pro-piracy]

Quote
my main source form here forward is: The Future of Music, by David Kusek and Gerd Leonhard. Rent it and read it if you still need convincing.

A lot of big stuffed shirts from record companies (Namely, the RIAA) try to tell you that music piracy, or as i like to call it, music sampling, is bad.

The Truth is, the RIAA and all their little friends know that piracy is not killing the industry. Its killing the recording industry, but definitely not the music industry. These big companies like RIAA want you to believe music piracy is bad so that they can make more money. And we all know that the RIAA is dirt poor, right?

Despite its bad-sounding name, piracy is actually quite good. Its completely free advertising for artists that gets their music heard and distributed. It has caused a massive interest in music among kids today, and though CD sales go down a little, concert sales have gone waaaaaay up. The thing is, why is it bad to be curious, to get a few free songs to find out what an artist is like, decide if you like them or not? There is nothing wrong with that! And its been going on since the days when people would trade vinyl to hear new things.

Now heres a metaphor: Say you got this new box of chocolate. Your friend has never tried chocolate before. You give your friend a peice of chocolate, and he enjoyed it. Now, the chocolate company is suing your friend for eating chocolate that belonged to them. That doesn't seem right, does it? YOU bought the box of chocolate, so its up to you if you want to share or not.

The same goes for music. Don't be afraid to share, you'll only be spreading the word of you favorite artist, making them more recognized.

Quote: Sniperwhere, January 01, 2008 05:51 pm

Quote: Sniperwhere, January 01, 2008 07:33 pm
Sounds interesting. But one thing I'm confused about is the scoring. You said that if you get a better time after the set ending time, that it counts as no demo posted. What do you mean by that?
He's using this rule because we're using Unreality's program, which incorporates highscoring and NUMA (It's very cool if haven't seen it yet.) Basically, you load a map from NUMA into the program using the map number. When it's loaded, a highscore board also appears that displays that top times submitted for this map. Whenever a run is submitted, it is also stamped with the time (of day) at which the person submitted it. All he is saying is that if you submit a new personal best after the deadline, it won't count, cause there's no way of knowing what your time was before.
That's a handfull. Do we need this program for the war?

Yes. And it's MUCH simpler than it looks.

#18989 1 2008-01-28T00:06:04Z T3chno
~T3chno's Photoshop Sig Guide!~

*Note*:
First off, this tutorial will not require any brushes, other than the ones already pre-installed with Photoshop.

With that, let's get started.
In this turotial, you will be making:




Open a new canvas. Use these demensions: 350x125. It's short, sweet, and to the point.

Next, find a render that you'll be using. This is the main focus of you sig. Go to Planetrenders.net and sign up to get access to a great amount of renders. The render I'm using is here.

Scale you render for the perfect size and paste it into your empty canvas.


Now what you want to do is duplicate the render several times.[Ctrl + A then Ctrl + C on one layer to duplicate it.] Spread the renders out so no white is seen.


Go to the top layer. Now merge the duplicated renders [Ctrl+E]. All the renders should be merged except for your original one.Then move your original render to the top.


Click on the layer which contains the duplicated renders. What you need are the .PSD's for 3 different sigs. PM me and I'll send you some if you don't have any. What you're going to do now is Filter -> Distort -> Displace.
Use the preset settings. Find your PSD. Click OK. Repeat this again with your two other .PSDs.


Duplicated the duplicated-renders layer (now renamed mergerenders]. On that duplicated layer, Filter->Distort->Ripple. Then on that same layer, Filter->Distort->ZigZag. Use the default settings on both. Set the layer to Lighten and merge it down.


Duplicate that layer again. Go to Filter->Brush Strokes->Spatter.Use default settings. Merge it down afterwards.


Okay, now what we're going to use is a C4D. This is the one I used: From Planetrenders.net
Place it in your sig's canvas. Place it nicely because this is key. Set the layer to lighten or luminosity or whatever fits nicely.


Go to Layer->New Adjustment Layer-> Gradient Map.


Then lower the opacity of that until it looks cool. (mine was around 66%.)


Go to Layer->New Adjustment Layer-> Brightness and contrast


Now do the Gradient map thing again. But instead of lowering the opacity, set it to Luminosity.


Now go to Layer ->Adjustment Layer-> Photo Filter


Okay, time to use our standard brush. Take out the 45 px. soft brush (the round fuzzy one). On a new layer on top, draw lines with that brush that go along with the flow of the sig. Make sure the color is white. Erase the lines that run over your render. Set that layer to overlay.


Now to darken parts of the sig to add a lighting effect. Take out the gradient tool and use the following settings.


Use the gradient on a new layer. Set it to soft light and reduce the opacity to make it look better.


Now to brighten it up a little. We're doing this back and forth stuff to add some texture depth to this sig. Go to Layer->New Adjustment Layer-> Curves


Now create a new layer. Then Image->Apply Image. Take out the Burn Tool and use it to darken areas that are too bright.


Now for lighting.Make a new layer. Take out the 65 px soft, white, fuzzy, round brush and make one line over the render that follows the sig's flow.


On that layer, Filter->Blur->Gaussion Blur. Set the blur so that it looks like a ray of light shining.


Erased the light over the render then reduce the opacity of the layer.


Okay, for the final touch of lighting. As you can tell, this render was originally in a picture where light was hitting it from the top right. But when this Autobot was rendered, that part was cut away. So time to add that light back in. (This works for some other renders too). Take a 100 px soft white brush and use one click to put it along the border, where you think the source of light is.


Make a new layer and Image->Apply Image. On this layer, Filter->Blur-> Motion Blur. Make the blur strokes follow your sig's flow and don't make the blur too intense.(45 pixels is a good blur distance)


Erase over the render and set the layer to Lighten.


Okay, almost done. Now, you may want to take out that burn tool and darken places that don't look good. Now you're ready for the text. I'm using a font called Technovia which can be found on the internet (Duh). Try http://dafont.com. Place your text in a nice spot. Set the text layer to Soft Light and duplicate it twice.


Now for the border! Create a new layer, Ctrl+A, then go to Edit->Stroke. Use these settings:


Now save it as .png, or whatever you wish. And you're done!
Final result:



Phew, that took a while.

~Inspired by different tutorials on the web.

I hope that helps at least someone with basic sig making in Photoshop.


~T3chno

Quote: Condog, February 12, 2008 09:22 pm
Love the second and the third. You have awesome background, where do you get them/how do you make them?

Well...

Copy paste the layer with the original render in it several times so there's no white space shown.
Merge all layers except for original render.
Filters->Displace :: 3 times with 3 different PSDs, try to have the PSD's not have any text in them
Filter -> Ripple :: Default settings
Filter -> Zig Zag :: Default settings
Brush strokes -> Spatter :: Default settings.

Now you have that background like so:

#19682 1 2008-03-25T01:51:49Z T3chno
I'm going to post a few questions here once in a while and I need your answers!

[From Chuck Klosterman's "Sex, Drugs and Cocoa Puffs: a Low Culture Manifesto."]

Some of these questions will be easy, and some hard....
Spoiler: 1.) You meet a wizard in downtown Chicago. The wizard tells you he can make you more attractive if you pay him money. When you ask how this process works, the wizard points to a random person on the street. You look at this random stranger. The wizard says, I will now make them a dollar more attractive. He waves his magic wand. Ostensibly, this person does not change at all; as far as you can tell, nothing is different. Butsomehowthis person is suddenly a little more appealing. The tangible difference is invisible to the naked eye, but you cant deny that this person is vaguely sexier. This wizard has a weird rule, thoughyou can only pay him once. You cant keep giving him money until youre satisfied. You can only pay him one lump sum up front. How much do you pay him?
Spoiler: 2.)You meet your soul mate. However, there is a catch: Every three years, someone will break both of your soul mate's collarbones with a Crescent wrench, and there is only one way you can stop this from happening: You must swallow a pill that will make every song you hear--for the rest of your life--sound as if it's being performed by the band Alice in Chains. When you hear Creedence Clearwater Revival on the radio, it will sound (to your ears) like it's being played by Alice in Chains. If you see Radiohead live, every one of their tunes will sound like it's being covered by Alice in Chains. When you hear a commercial jingle on TV, it will sound like Alice in Chains; if you sing to yourself in the shower, your voice will sound like deceased Alice vocalist Layne Staley performing a capella (but it will only sound this way to you).

Would you swallow the pill?
Spoiler: 3.)Defying all expectation, a group of Scottish marine biologists capture a live Loch Ness Monster. In an almost unbelievable coincidence, a bear hunter in the Pacific Northwest shoots a Sasquatch in the thigh, thereby allowing zoologists to take the furry monster into captivity. These events happen on the same afternoon. That evening, the president announces he may have thyroid cancer and will undergo a biopsy later that week.

You are the front page editor of The New York Times: What do you play as the biggest story?
Spoiler: 4.)Genetic engineers at Johns Hopkins University announce that they have developed a so-called "super gorilla." Though the animal cannot speak, it has a sign language lexicon of over twelve thousand words, an I.Q. of almost 85, and--most notably--a vague sense of self-awareness. Oddly, the creature (who weighs seven hundred pounds) becomes fascinated by football. The gorilla aspires to play the game at its highest level and quickly develops the rudimentary skills of a defensive end. ESPN analyst Tom Jackson speculates that this gorilla would be "borderline unblockable" and would likely average six sacks a game (although Jackson concedes the beast might be susceptible to counters and misdirection plays). It is also clear that the gorilla would never intentionally harm an opponent.

You are commissioner of the NFL: Would you allow this gorilla to sign with the Oakland Raiders?
Spoiler: 5.)A novel titled Interior Mirror is released to mammoth commercial success (despite middling reviews). However, a curious social trend emerges: Though no one can prove a direct scientific link, it appears that almost 30 percent of the people who read this book immediately become homosexual. Many of these newfound homosexuals credit the book for helping them reach this conclusion about their orientation, despite the fact that Interior Mirror is ostensibly a crime novel with no homoerotic content (and was written by a straight man).

Would this phenomenon increase (or decrease) the likelihood of you reading this book?
Spoiler: 6.)Let us assume you met a rudimentary magician. Let us assume he can do five simple tricks-he can pull a rabbit out of his hat, he can make a coin disappear, he can turn the ace of spades into the Joker card, and two others in a similar vein. These are his only tricks and he can't learn any more; he can only do these five. HOWEVER, it turns out he's doing these five tricks with real magic. It's not an illusion; he can actually conjure the bunny out of the ether and he can move the coin through space. He's legitimately magical, but extremely limited in scope and influence.

Would this person be more impressive than Albert Einstein?
Spoiler: 7.)At long last, someone invents "the dream VCR." This machine allows you to tape an entire evening's worth of your own dreams, which you can then watch at your leisure. However, the inventor of the dream VCR will only allow you to use this device of you agree to a strange caveat: When you watch your dreams, you must do so with your family and your closest friends in the same room. They get to watch your dreams along with you. And if you don't agree to this, you can't use the dream VCR.

Would you still do this?
Spoiler: 8.)You are watching a movie in a crowded theater. Though the plot is mediocre, you find yourself dazzled by the special effects. But with twenty minutes left in the film, you are struck with an undeniable feeling of doom: You are suddenly certain your mother has just died. There is no logical reason for this to be true, but you are certain of it. You are overtaken with the irrational metaphysical sense that. Somewhere . Your mom has just perished. But this is only an intuitive, amorphous feeling; there is no evidence for this, and your mother has not been ill.

Would you immediately exit the theater, or would you finish watching the movie?
Spoiler: 9.)Every person you have ever slept with is invited to a banquet where you are the guest of honor. No one will be in attendance except you, the collection of your former lovers, and the catering service. After the meal, you are asked to give a fifteen-minute speech to the assembly.

What do you talk about?
Spoiler: 10.)This is the opening line of Jay McInerneys Bright Lights, Big City: You are not the kind of guy who would be in a place like this at this time of the morning. Think about that line in the context of the novel (assuming youve read it). Now go to your CD collection and find Hearts Little Queen album (assuming you own it). Listen to the opening riff to Barracuda.

Which of these two introductions is a higher form of art?
Spoiler: 11.) Let us assume a fully grown, completely healthy Clydesdale horse has his hooves shackled to the ground while his head is held in place with thick rope. He is conscious and standing upright, but completely immobile. And let us assume that--for some reason--every *POLITICAL* prisoner on earth (as cited by Amnesty International) will be released from captivity if you can kick this horse to death in less than twenty minutes. You are allowed to wear steel-toed boots.

Would you attempt to do this?
Spoiler: 12.)You meet the perfect person. Romantically, this person is ideal: You find them physically attractive, intellectually stimulating, consistently funny, and deeply compassionate. However, they have one quirk: This individual is obsessed with Jim Hensons gothic puppet fantasy The Dark Crystal. Beyond watching it on DVD at least once a month, he/she peppers casual conversation with Dark Crystal references, uses Dark Crystal analogies to explain everyday events, and occasionally likes to talk intensely about the films deeper philosophy.

Would this be enough to stop you from marrying this individual?
Spoiler: 13.)Let us assume there are two boxes on a table. In one box, there is a relatively normal turtle; in the other, Adolf Hitler's skull. You have to select one of these items for your home. If you select the turtle, you can't give it away and you have to keep it alive for two years; if either of these parameters are not met, you will be fined $999 by the state. If you select Hitler's skull, you are required to display it in a semi-prominent location in your living room for the same amount of time, although you will be paid a stipend of $120 per month for doing so. Display of the skull must be apolitical.

Which option do you select?
Spoiler: 14.)For reasons that cannot be explained, cats can suddenly read at a twelfth-grade level. They cant talk and they cant write, but they can read silently and understand the text. Many cats love this new skill, because they now have something to do all day while they lay around the house; however, a few cats become depressed, because reading forces them to realize the limitations of their existence (not to mention the utter frustration of being unable to express themselves).

This being the case, do you think the average cat would enjoy Garfield, or would cats find this cartoon to be an insulting caricature?

You. Hurt. My. Brain.

Chrono Trigger was one of the best and most popular RPGs on the Super Nintendo. (And that's saying a lot when we're talking abuot the system that housed such RPG giants as Final Fantasy 2 and 3, Earthbound, Secret of Mana and Mario RPG, to name a few.)

The combat has an active battle system - the kind where each player has a bar that fills up over time, and they can take an action when it's full. Faster characters fill their bars faster. It's not pure turn-based fighting, but it's far from the real-time action of Kingdom Hearts.

If you've never played Chrono Trigger, you're missing out on a great gaming experience. Actually, based on the way you asked about it, I'm guessing you haven't played a lot of Super Nintendo games. So here's what I'm going to recommend: Look around at some garage sales, swap meets and independent game stores until you find a Super Nintendo system (I can't imagine one costing more than $20 these days), buy it, and come back to us for the list of games you should buy. Again, they'll be cheap. Maybe $3 each, $7 for the expensive ones. For starters, Zelda: A Link to the Past, Super Metroid, Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy III, Super Mario World. You'll get the console and half a dozen five-star games for the price of one new DS title.

QFE.

The game/card store I live across has a Super Nintendo on sale for $15. Good deal, as it comes with two controllers as well. Condition is great too. They have a ton of games for ~$5 each. The N64 is $30 there, but it's all beat up.

But seriously, if you haven't played this game, you've missed out on so much.

Well, it looks good. i don't like JRPGs much, but if it's anything like Kingdom Hearts, I'm definitely getting it.

You. Hurt. My. Brain.

Chrono Trigger was one of the best and most popular RPGs on the Super Nintendo. (And that's saying a lot when we're talking abuot the system that housed such RPG giants as Final Fantasy 2 and 3, Earthbound, Secret of Mana and Mario RPG, to name a few.)

The combat has an active battle system - the kind where each player has a bar that fills up over time, and they can take an action when it's full. Faster characters fill their bars faster. It's not pure turn-based fighting, but it's far from the real-time action of Kingdom Hearts.

If you've never played Chrono Trigger, you're missing out on a great gaming experience. Actually, based on the way you asked about it, I'm guessing you haven't played a lot of Super Nintendo games. So here's what I'm going to recommend: Look around at some garage sales, swap meets and independent game stores until you find a Super Nintendo system (I can't imagine one costing more than $20 these days), buy it, and come back to us for the list of games you should buy. Again, they'll be cheap. Maybe $3 each, $7 for the expensive ones. For starters, Zelda: A Link to the Past, Super Metroid, Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy III, Super Mario World. You'll get the console and half a dozen five-star games for the price of one new DS title.
Wow, LV. I never knew you were so passionate about this. The game sounds good, and that kind of combat system is great, a I /hate/ turned based JRPGs. And, I've heard that there were a lot of awesome Super Nintendo games out there, but those were before I was old enough to appreciate them. I have an N64, but it's broken, and I don't know if I can fix it. Again. I'm going to do a Google search for them in my area, but I probably won't turn up much. We live in a mostly secluded area. By the way, I've never played Metroid, (regularly anyway. I've only played it once or twice.) any Zelda game, (besides Phantom Hourglass, which is very fun. I recommend it to anyone who liked Wind Waker, but the combat style's been revamped. Kinda.), and I've only played Mario once or twice. So, as you can see, my career in gaming's not my best. But, it seems that I'll have to make up for it now.

How can you appreciate the hype about Zelda games if you don't know their roots.

I understand Kingdom Hearts is an amazing game with a fantastic storyline, but it's impact on gaming will never be at par with that of the original Mario games.

#457915 7 2008-08-03T19:17:38Z T3chno
Hm, looks like my old stuff in some way. My thoughts:
*Get rid of scan lines. All of them. They are so 2007.
*Keep brush use to a limit. Your background should not be 100% brushes.
*Use new techniques in your sigs, such as smudging, C4Ds, etc.
*Keep colors varied. All red is consistent, but it's better to have variations of red.
*Depth. All you did was paste a render and put scan lines on them. No. You have to make them part of the sig.
*Blur tool: To add more depth to the sig, blur parts of a sig to make it seem like it's farther away.
*Follow tutorials: Depending on what imaging program you have, you can find loads of tuts by Googling. If you have Photoshop, bonzai collecting numerouss tutorial links here.

Hope to some more work from you. The best way to improve is to keep making sigs and experimenting.

#471945 13 2008-09-20T21:32:13Z T3chno
Quote: Hendor, September 20, 2008 01:20 pm
Quote: T3chno, September 19, 2008 10:39 pm
Was it AB that was the universal donor and O the universal acceptor?

No, it's the other way around. Read on.


Your blood type refers to which type of antigens and antibodies are found in the blood. An antigen is simply an identifier, while it is an antibody's job to attack certain things it believes to be harmful. People with blood type A have A antigens and anti-B antibodies. If they are given blood from someone with blood type B, their anti-B antibodies will reject it. Basically what this means is that you can't get blood that has antibodies against your blood type. So... people with the blood type AB can get blood from anyone because their blood has both A and B antigens and NO antibodies, or else their blood would attack itself. Because it has no antibodies, it is impossible for it to attack anything. Conversely, type O is the universal donor, because it has NO antigens and both A and B antibodies. Therefore, no blood type will attack it, because it simply can't identify it.

A common question after hearing this is "Why don't the anti-A antibodies in type O blood attack type A blood when the type O is transfused into type A." This question makes sense because type A blood has A antigens, so why don't the anti-A antibodies in the O blood attack them? The answer is that blood antibodies are found in the blood plasma, as opposed to the antigens on the surface of the red blood cells. The plasma is not included in a transfusion.

Sorry for the long winded answer, but I've just recently learned this and was testing myself. I'm type A, don't know the Rh.

Mmmyeah. I remembered after Tsukatu's post. We did a lab in freshman year where we had four blood samples (or liquids with similar characteristics) and we determined if A would accept B, etc.
